newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian forint ends weaker vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian forint ends weaker vs dollar.

text.p: The Hungarian forint closed weaker against the dollar on Friday in routine trade as it tracked the dollar/mark on international markets, dealers said.

The Hungarian forint closed at 171.75/80 against the U.S. unit, compared to 171.50/55 at the opening, they said, adding that the forint ended close to the National Bank of Hungary's resistance level (bid).

"The forint almost closed the 10-pip gap that separated it from the central bank bid earlier today," said Peter Luczo of Inter-Europa Bank. The National Bank of Hungary fixed the forint at 171.70 to one dollar, down from 170.95 on Thursday.
Traders believe that with liquidity stable on the money markets, rates on the spot forex market are unlikely to be affected by the tax payment deadline on Monday.
The Swiss franc dominated curremcy futures trade on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE), accounting for over half the relatively low 2.3 billion forints' turnover.
Most significant movements were in the dollar, which fell for most contracts and the mark, which rose for four maturities. The yen and sterling were mixed while the Ecu and lira were stable.
